detailed_rationale:
Raymond Lifestyle is the branded-apparel and lifestyle business (Raymond, Park Avenue, ColorPlus, Ethnix, and the Raymond retail network) that was demerged from the erstwhile Raymond Limited, with the group's real estate business (Raymond Realty) and engineering business separated into their own listed entities as part of the same 'Raymond 2.0' restructuring completed through 2025. Revenue growth has been genuinely strong -- Q4 FY26 net sales of Rs 1,776.45 crore were up 18.89% YoY, and full-year total income of Rs 7,034 crore was up 11% YoY, with full-year EBITDA up 23% to Rs 804 crore (margin improving to 11.4% from 10.2%). But quarter-to-quarter profitability has been volatile and, in the most recent quarter, negative: Q4 FY26 posted a net loss of Rs 52.06 crore (PAT margin -2.93%), a sharp reversal from a Rs 42.86 crore profit in Q3 FY26 and a wider loss than the Rs 44.95 crore loss in the year-ago Q4. PBDIT margin (excluding other income) fell to 6.67% in Q4 from 12.82% in Q3. For the full year the company stayed narrowly profitable (Rs 46.17 crore versus Rs 38.19 crore in FY25), so the FY26 numbers are 'profitable but barely, and getting more volatile, not less.'

On governance, a promoter-group pledge exists (J.K. Investors reduced its Raymond Lifestyle pledge to 8.35% of share capital in May 2026 after having pledged and released shares across the group's listed entities during the demerger period) -- moderate and trending down, not a standalone red flag, but worth noting given the multiple recent corporate actions across the group's newly separated entities. At a trailing PE near 96x, the market is paying a growth-stock multiple for a business whose quarterly earnings just swung to a loss.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score is Sell on both horizons (24.97 / 33.89) with a balance-sheet flag of AMBER. Revenue growth is real, but profitability is both thin (sub-1% full-year PAT margin) and volatile (a swing from profit to loss quarter-on-quarter), and the ~96x trailing multiple already prices a level of margin durability the company has not yet demonstrated. That combination does not support a rescue.
summary: Raymond Lifestyle is the branded-apparel business (Raymond, Park Avenue, ColorPlus, and related brands) spun out as part of the wider Raymond Group's three-way demerger completed in 2025. Revenue is growing at a healthy double-digit pace, but profitability remains thin and volatile -- the company swung to a loss in the most recent quarter after a profitable prior quarter -- and the stock's current valuation already prices in a level of earnings stability the business has not consistently shown yet.
positive_para: Revenue growth has been consistently strong across recent quarters (Q4 FY26 net sales +18.89% YoY, full-year +11%), full-year EBITDA grew 23% with margin expansion to 11.4%, and the post-demerger, focused branded-apparel structure (with real estate and engineering now separately listed) gives management a cleaner mandate to run the lifestyle business on its own merits.
negative_para: Quarterly profitability is genuinely volatile: a Rs 42.86 crore Q3 FY26 profit reversed into a Rs 52.06 crore Q4 FY26 loss, with PBDIT margin (ex-other income) nearly halving sequentially to 6.67%. Full-year PAT margin is under 1% of revenue, leaving very little cushion, and at a trailing PE near 96x the market is already paying for consistent, durable earnings that the last two quarters have not delivered. A promoter pledge (8.35% of share capital as of May 2026) is trending down but is still part of the picture during a period of multiple corporate actions across the demerged group entities.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A trailing PE near 96x on a business with a sub-1% full-year net margin and a quarter that just swung to a loss implies the market is valuing this almost entirely on the EBITDA growth trajectory (+23% FY26) and the demerger-driven focus story, not on current bottom-line earnings power. That is a defensible growth narrative, but the multiple leaves very little room for execution missteps, and the last two quarters (profit to loss) are exactly the kind of volatility that multiple assumes will not recur.
